aToIEditing.note: the run's node is the Reactome pathway name 'Formation of editosomes by ADAR proteins'; its mechanism calls them 'editosomes that mediate RNA editing' and its title 'impaired RNA editing'. No GO process for ADAR editosome assembly; GO:0045293 'mRNA editing complex' (synonym editosome) is a component defined as an insertion/deletion editing complex, so not used. The editosome is the mechanism of A-to-I editing named in passing: one node.

hyp1.note: the title names ADAR loss-of-function variants, but the chain starts at the ADAR gene, so the claim is about ADAR; 'loss of function drives psoriasis' gives neg. The title's target is 'an interferon-dependent psoriasis subtype'; there is no MONDO term for it, so psoriasis.

hyp2.no_claim_reason: no direction for EIF2AK4: the title says its variants 'modulate' psoriasis risk and the mechanism says the pathway 'influences' IL-17A; the mechanism's 'decreased risk' is for rs182525087, whose cited row names no allele ('rs182525087-?'); every step is associated_with with polarity unknown

findings.detail: hyp1's title ('ADAR loss-of-function variants drive an interferon-dependent psoriasis subtype through impaired RNA editing') restates the title of its own citation PMID:42424135 (2026); it is a published finding, not a new hypothesis.

Rated low confidence and 'speculative', though its one paper reports four multiplex families with cosegregating ADAR1 loss-of-function variants, six more rare variants in a 125-patient cohort, and cell-level rescue; the run under-rates its best-supported claim.

PMID:42424135 states ADAR1 knockdown raises IFN-stimulated genes and that ADAR1 loss-of-function variants cosegregate with psoriasis, but the chain uses neither direct link and instead routes through 'formation of editosomes', a node the paper never names.

R-HSA-77042 is an over-representation result with 1 of the pathway's 2 entities matched: a pathway named after ADAR proteins is 'enriched' because ADAR is in the gene set, so the FDR adds nothing; the record states no step and is excluded as enrichment.

Neither citation states that editing or editosome formation inhibits IFN signalling: PMID:42424135 reports reduced editing and raised IFN-stimulated genes as parallel outcomes of ADAR1 knockdown, and R-HSA-913531 is a gene-set enrichment; the one inhibitory step in hyp1's arm has no evidence.

The chain nodes 'Formation of editosomes' and 'Interferon Signaling' are Reactome pathway names lifted from enrichment results, not entities the literature citations use (the paper speaks of A-to-I RNA editing and IFN-stimulated genes).
Every chain node except psoriasis has an empty curie and grounding_evidence, including the genes ADAR and EIF2AK4 and the context cell type.
'immune cell metabolic rewiring' is too vague to ground: no named metabolic process, cell type or direction.

The step is stitched from two papers neither of which names both ends: PMID:23216249 is about GCN2 amino-acid sensing in dietary-restriction longevity (no immune cells), PMID:33613560 about diet rewiring immune-cell metabolism (no GCN2).

PMID:40073267 is about the CCR6-CCL20 axis driving IL-17 in murine epidermal gamma-delta T cells under obesity; it never mentions EIF2AK4/GCN2, so the step's note ('associated with IL-17A production in epidermal T cells during psoriasis') has no source.

All three steps start at EIF2AK4: 'immune cell metabolic rewiring' and 'IL-17A production' are dead ends that never connect to each other or to psoriasis, so the 'chain' is three separate associations, not a mechanism.

The mechanism says rs182525087 is 'significantly associated with a decreased risk of psoriasis', but the cited row has p = 4e-6 with genomeWide False, from one East Asian study (GCST90435380) with no replication sample.
The row's risk allele is 'rs182525087-?' (riskFrequency NR), so the beta's 'decrease' belongs to no named allele, and 'decreased risk' cannot be attached to any allele or to EIF2AK4.

The record's genomic contexts put rs182525087 in an intron of GPR176 (distance 0); EIF2AK4 is about 46.8 kb away and not flagged closest gene, so tying the hit to EIF2AK4 rests only on the row's 'mapped gene' label.

Every hyp2 step is associated_with with polarity unknown and the title says only 'modulate', yet the falsification expects EIF2AK4 knockout to lower IL-17A, a direction the chain never states or cites.
The only citation for the epidermal gamma-delta T cell step is a mouse study (murine wound healing and psoriasis models).

The abstention cites GWAS:ZBP1/DVL2/KHK:no-association, PMID:PPR1233591 and CXG:MONDO_0005083:no-cohort, none of which is in sources.json, so its claims (including that keratinocyte PANoptosis in psoriasis is ZBP1-independent) cannot be checked.
Three GWAS no-association records (ZBP1, DVL2, KHK) are used to say the GWAS Catalog 'explicitly confirms an absence of associated variants' for all 13 remaining genes.

The run's own enrichment R-HSA-913531 matched 4 gene-set members to Interferon Signaling, but hyp1 uses only ADAR and the abstention says the remaining genes form no coherent network without saying which other members matched or why they were set aside.

Both hypotheses list empty supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence and the run cites no contradicting source, although the abstention shows the agent did find refuting literature for another gene (ZBP1).

A Reactome over-representation record whose only content is the pathway name fits both the guide's `enrichment` exclusion and `curatedDb` (Reactome membership); no rule says which wins. The curator kept it as curatedDb; the audit excluded it as enrichment, as every other run does, since the row does not name the matched gene.

'Formation of editosomes' grounded to GO:0006382 (adenosine to inosine editing): GO has no process for ADAR editosome assembly and GO:0045293 'mRNA editing complex' (synonym editosome) is defined as an insertion/deletion complex; Reactome:R-HSA-77042 was the other option, and the choice decides whether the paper's 'reduced adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing' supports hyp1.1.

'Functional studies showed that ADAR1 knockdown or expression of ... alleles' does not name the system (cells or animals); recorded inVitro, but the abstract alone cannot settle inVitro vs mechanistic.

'define a novel IFN-dependent psoriasis subtype' is the authors' conclusion over family genetics, single-cell data and cell rescue; there is no kind for a mixed-design conclusion, so I recorded observational (nothing tests IFN causing disease).

No form for a disease subtype defined by genotype and mechanism ('IFN-dependent psoriasis' in ADAR1 loss-of-function carriers): no MONDO term, and refining psoriasis by a condition would disconnect hyp1.3 from the claim's target, so the subtype evidence counts for psoriasis at large.
observational evidence carries no field for significance, replication or allele: a sub-threshold row (p = 4e-6, genomeWide False, allele '?') weighs the same as a replicated genome-wide hit.

No rule for a gene-level association step backed by a variant row whose own genomic context places the variant in another gene (GPR176); I kept the row because it names EIF2AK4 as mapped gene, and recorded the doubt.
A hypothesis whose steps are all unsigned associations gets no claim and no arm, so BioLean records nothing about its overall weight even though one step (hyp2.3) has a kept citation.

The corpus definition of GO:0140888 'interferon-mediated signaling pathway' (synonym 'interferon signaling pathway') says 'initiated by type II interferon binding', contradicting its generic label; the node is used for the run's generic 'Interferon Signaling', while the paper's signal is type I IFN, so any textbook bridge quoted from it would be wrong.

render.py renders only sign_note: the 'note' keys on S3, S5 and the aToIEditing entity (subtype scope, sub-threshold GWAS row in GPR176, editosome merge) never reach the Lean module, so the caveats that qualify those statements are lost downstream.

Every kept citation for hyp1 comes from one 2026 abstract (PMID:42424135, cited once); its other two sources (R-HSA-77042, R-HSA-913531) are enrichment rows that state no step, so the budget's min_sources_per_hypothesis of 2 is met only by counting them.

The proposed falsification (ADAR knockdown to see if it hyperactivates interferon signalling and inflammatory cytokines) is what the cited PMID:42424135 already reports ('ADAR1 knockdown ... increased IFN-stimulated genes and inflammatory cytokines'), so it is not a test of a new claim.
The question's budget sets min_hypotheses 3; the run returns 2 hypotheses (one of which, hyp2, is not a connected chain) and abstains for the other 13 genes.

The abstention sets aside IFNW1 (UniProt:P05000, interferon omega-1, a type I interferon) as having no shared mechanism, although hyp1's own mechanism is an 'aberrant interferon response' and the run itself found 'Interferon Signaling' enriched (R-HSA-913531, 4 entities matched, members not named); the run does not say why IFNW1 has no part in hyp1.

audit.before: kept as evidence, kind curatedDb, quote 'Formation of editosomes by ADAR proteins'
audit.reason: The record is a Reactome over-representation row ('over-represented in this gene set: 1 of 2 pathway entities matched'). It does not say which gene matched, and a pathway name is not a statement that ADAR is needed for A-to-I editing. The curator excluded the run's other Reactome row (R-HSA-913531) as enrichment, and every other curated run excludes such rows the same way. S1 is no longer 'established' (it was belief 5/6) on a circular enrichment hit; its only support is the paper's in vitro span.

The text does state IL-17 production by epidermal gamma-delta T cells, but for CCL20/CCR6 ('CCL20 stimulates epidermal γδ T cells to produce interleukin (IL)-17'), not EIF2AK4: the step for a different gene.
